<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Implement an unsigned 8bit multiplier based on pipelining processing.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal that controls the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="MUL_WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="MUL_OUT_WIDTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_en_out_reg">
            <description>mul_en_out_reg is a 3-bit register that stores the input enable signal mul_en_in. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 on the negative edge of the reset signal.</description>
            <update_event>on positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n</update_event>
            <update_action>
                <if>
                    <condition>rst_n == 0</condition>
                    <then>
                        <assign>mul_en_out_reg = 3'b000;</assign>
                    </then>
                    <else>
                        <assign>mul_en_out_reg = {mul_en_out_reg[1:0], mul_en_in};</assign>
                    </else>
                </if>
            </update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="mul_en_out">
            <description>mul_en_out is an output signal that indicates if the multiplication operation is enabled. It is derived from the most significant bit of mul_en_out_reg.</description>
            <output>mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg[2];</output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_a_reg">
            <description>mul_a_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input multiplicand signal mul_a. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 on the negative edge of the reset signal.</description>
            <update_event>on positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n</update_event>
            <update_action>
                <if>
                    <condition>rst_n == 0</condition>
                    <then>
                        <assign>mul_a_reg = 8'b00000000;</assign>
                    </then>
                    <else>
                        <assign>mul_a_reg = mul_a;</assign>
                    </else>
                </if>
            </update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_b_reg">
            <description>mul_b_reg is a 8-bit register that stores the input multiplier signal mul_b. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 on the negative edge of the reset signal.</description>
            <update_event>on positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n</update_event>
            <update_action>
                <if>
                    <condition>rst_n == 0</condition>
                    <then>
                        <assign>mul_b_reg = 8'b00000000;</assign>
                    </then>
                    <else>
                        <assign>mul_b_reg = mul_b;</assign>
                    </else>
                </if>
            </update_action>
        </sequential_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="temp">
            <description>temp is a 8-bit wide wire array that stores the partial products generated by the bitwise AND operations between the bits of mul_a_reg and the corresponding bits of mul_b_reg. Each element of the array corresponds to a partial product generated by a specific bit of mul_b_reg.</description>
            <output>
                <assign>temp[0] = mul_b_reg[0] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
                <assign>temp[1] = mul_b_reg[1] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
                <assign>temp[2] = mul_b_reg[2] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
                <assign>temp[3] = mul_b_reg[3] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
                <assign>temp[4] = mul_b_reg[4] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
                <assign>temp[5] = mul_b_reg[5] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
                <assign>temp[6] = mul_b_reg[6] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
                <assign>temp[7] = mul_b_reg[7] ? mul_a_reg : 8'b00000000;</assign>
            </output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <combinational_logic id="sum">
            <description>sum is a 16-bit wide wire array that stores the partial sums generated by the addition of the partial products. Each element of the array corresponds to a partial sum generated by a specific group of partial products.</description>
            <output>
                <assign>sum[0] = temp[0][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[1] = temp[0][1] + temp[1][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[2] = temp[0][2] + temp[1][1] + temp[2][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[3] = temp[0][3] + temp[1][2] + temp[2][1] + temp[3][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[4] = temp[0][4] + temp[1][3] + temp[2][2] + temp[3][1] + temp[4][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[5] = temp[0][5] + temp[1][4] + temp[2][3] + temp[3][2] + temp[4][1] + temp[5][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[6] = temp[0][6] + temp[1][5] + temp[2][4] + temp[3][3] + temp[4][2] + temp[5][1] + temp[6][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[7] = temp[0][7] + temp[1][6] + temp[2][5] + temp[3][4] + temp[4][3] + temp[5][2] + temp[6][1] + temp[7][0];</assign>
                <assign>sum[8] = temp[1][7] + temp[2][6] + temp[3][5] + temp[4][4] + temp[5][3] + temp[6][2] + temp[7][1];</assign>
                <assign>sum[9] = temp[2][7] + temp[3][6] + temp[4][5] + temp[5][4] + temp[6][3] + temp[7][2];</assign>
                <assign>sum[10] = temp[3][7] + temp[4][6] + temp[5][5] + temp[6][4] + temp[7][3];</assign>
                <assign>sum[11] = temp[4][7] + temp[5][6] + temp[6][5] + temp[7][4];</assign>
                <assign>sum[12] = temp[5][7] + temp[6][6] + temp[7][5];</assign>
                <assign>sum[13] = temp[6][7] + temp[7][6];</assign>
                <assign>sum[14] = temp[7][7];</assign>
                <assign>sum[15] = 0;</assign>
            </output>
        </combinational_logic>
        <sequential_logic id="mul_out_reg">
            <description>mul_out_reg is a 16-bit register that stores the final product of the multiplication operation. It is updated on the positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 on the negative edge of the reset signal.</description>
            <update_event>on positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n</update_event>
            <update_action>
                <if>
                    <condition>rst_n == 0</condition>
                    <then>
                        <assign>mul_out_reg = 16'b0000000000000000;</
